clue.text: Stop being loyal

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, especially of blood, is to stem it; this verb is an old spelling of stanch
as an adjective the word means steadfastly faithful

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their allegiance and gives up being loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to stem a flow, and the adjective sense is steadfast, true and faithful.

clue.text: Dish one breaks into pieces

definitions.meaning: a dish is an attractive person
something that breaks things into pieces

explanation.surface: Someone drops a plate that shatters.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang word for an attractive person, and literally one who shatters things.

clue.text: Petulant and in a flap before marriage

indicators.note: a flap is a state of agitation, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy and agitated in the run-up to a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' only joins the fodder words Petulant and 'in a', which 'flap' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means happening or made before marriage, as in a prenuptial agreement.

clue.text: Little lump of bread taken over to rubbish container

indicators.note: taken over means turned over, reversed in a down clue

parts.note: a bun is a small bread roll
a bin holds rubbish

explanation.surface: A small lump of bread is taken to the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A small knob or stub, a small lump of something.

clue.text: Given destructive piece of criticism, axe post

parts.note: a hatchet is a small axe
a post is a job

explanation.surface: After a scathing review, someone loses their position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is a link: the definition is given by the wordplay that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe and malicious attack on someone's reputation in writing, a savage criticism.

clue.text: Splendid —- unputdownable after good start

indicators.note: what is left after the opening letter is dropped, so the word loses its head

parts.note: an unputdownable book is gripping

indicators.note: start picks the opening letter of the word good

explanation.surface: A reviewer praises a splendid novel that hooks the reader from its strong opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after good start' means the synonym for unputdownable once its first letter, the G that starts 'good', has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is old-fashioned British slang for excellent or first-rate, a synonym of splendid.

clue.text: Girl losing grand in game

indicators.note: losing means the letter is taken out

parts.note: rugby is a game
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A girl loses a thousand pounds gambling on a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Call girl's criminal record on a standard document

parts.note: a pro is a prostitute, with the possessive giving no letter
form is slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: A prostitute's criminal record is entered on an official form.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of a standard kind used as a template, like an invoice issued in advance.

clue.text: Sort of barrister that lost his head

indicators.note: lost his head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a silk is a senior barrister, a Queen's Counsel, who wears a silk gown

explanation.surface: A lawyer of a certain kind lost his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means kind or type, as in people of that ilk.

clue.text: Boy gripped by French author in French department

indicators.note: the boy is held inside the author's name

parts.note: Andre Gide was a French novelist
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy is held by a French writer in a part of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Gironde is one of the administrative departments of France, around Bordeaux.

clue.text: What Bill will possibly be doing

definitions.text: What Bill will possibly be doing

parts.words: What Bill will possibly be doing
parts.note: a parliamentary bill, once passed, becomes law under a new name; the surface pretends Bill is a man performing on stage

explanation.surface: A man named Bill wonders what he will be doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary bill that is passed becomes a statute of that name, and to perform on stage is also this verb.

clue.text: Drug (pill found by bar) dropped in drink

indicators.note: the pill and bar are put inside the drink, as a pill is dropped into a glass

parts.note: beer is a drink
a tab is a pill or tablet
to lock is to bar a door

explanation.surface: Someone slips a pill into a drink at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A beta-blocker is a medicine that slows the heart, so it is a kind of drug.

clue.text: Could one be friends with woman before match?

definitions.text: Could one be friends with woman before match?

parts.words: Could one be friends with woman before match?
parts.note: match is a wedding, and the friends are a bride's party out together the evening before; hen is British slang for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to befriend a woman ahead of a sports fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a bride and her female friends hold a party the night before the wedding, which is the match.

clue.text: Criticise cheat

definitions.meaning: to swindle or get the better of someone unfairly

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone has been unfairly running down and swindling others.
explanation.definitionFit: This British phrasal verb means both to speak badly of someone and to swindle them.

clue.text: Novel, unusual sort with evil wit, is …

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters taken in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A novel about an odd character with a wicked wit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'is' are links; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's novel about an orphan in workhouse and London crime is a classic of fiction.

clue.text: … a book I rate — novel sort

indicators.note: sort means sort out, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Someone rates a book highly as a novel of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Revelation is the final book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Transported by river? That's likely

parts.note: apt means likely, as in apt to happen

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether goods will probably be carried by boat along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Transported here means carried away with delight, enthralled or entranced.

clue.text: Well ahead of course to make more efficient

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in front of the second

parts.note: to well is to flow out, to stream
a line is a course or route

explanation.surface: Advice to go well before the main event to improve efficiency.
explanation.definitionFit: To simplify a process or organisation is to make it run more efficiently.

clue.text: After short revolution workers could be seizing a plant

indicators.note: the combined pieces seize the letter a, holding it inside
the workers come after the shortened revolution
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a cycle is one revolution
men are workers

explanation.surface: After a brief uprising, workers might grab a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclamen is a flowering plant with swept-back petals.

clue.text: Regular exercises one did with lazy jerks

indicators.note: jerks suggests letters jolted about, signalling a rearrangement of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone lazy performed the routine with lazy, jerky movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the fodder words one, did and lazy, which 'jerks' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old British phrase for a set of physical exercises done every morning as routine.

clue.text: Object one's at first successfully hidden in nick

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the nick

parts.note: a dent is a nick or notch
one is I, and 's is is, giving IS

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A protester's objection is successfully concealed in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to dissent, disagreeing with an official view.

clue.text: Hide from attack

definitions.meaning: an animal skin with its fur

explanation.surface: Someone advises taking cover from an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal skin is a pelt, and to pelt is to bombard with thrown objects.

clue.text: Cover to protect bun or tart

indicators.note: the cover protects the bun by going around it

parts.note: a top is a cover or lid
a roll is a bun

explanation.surface: A baker covers a bun or tart to keep it fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart is slang for a promiscuous woman, as is this old word.

clue.text: When it's rare for three to be behind?

annotationWithheld.clue: When it's rare for three to be behind?

clue.text: Just being cunning about what's said to encourage performer

indicators.note: the cunning word goes round the shout

parts.note: sly means cunning
ole is the shout of encouragement to a bullfighter or flamenco dancer

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of slyly flattering an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in the sense of only or exclusively, as in just for fun.

clue.text: Voice one's raised in row on river

indicators.note: the row is placed on, following, the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a row or quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone's voice rises in an argument on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a high singing voice that a male singer produces above his normal range, so it is raised.

clue.text: Pass a swimmer in the sea

explanation.surface: Someone swims past another bather in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A goby is a small marine fish, and the phrase also means to pass by.

clue.text: Without working premise to make up?

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: working suggests letters being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone must make it up as they go, without a premise to work from.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise, inventing something on the spot without preparation, is to make it up.

clue.text: Starting to save money

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Starting to save money' has no parse giving TIN with every word used: 'Starting' has no job; the scan is blank, so a misread cannot be confirmed.

clue.text: Poor horse avoided climb

indicators.note: avoided means the horse's letter is left out

parts.note: a hill is a climb
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A weak horse refused to go up the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor in the sense of unwell or in bad health, as in poor health.

clue.text: Extremely Tudoresque French city residence

indicators.note: extremely takes the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: Nancy is a city in eastern France

explanation.surface: A mock-Tudor house in a French city is a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenancy is occupancy of a home or land as a tenant, a period of residence.

clue.text: After dropping ecstasy gas a great deal, spinning endlessly

indicators.note: the gas has the drug's letter dropped from it

parts.note: neon is a gas
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: spinning turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: pots means a great deal, as in pots of money

explanation.surface: After giving up drugs, someone talks gas endlessly and their head is spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Without stopping, continuously, is the same as endlessly.
